method: front-master-only component-first side reconstruction; do not condition on rejected whole side image

arguments.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept / mechanical cross-view design correction. The ONLY attached reference is the current Social Brave King FRONT THREE-QUARTER MASTER. Treat it as the design authority. Do NOT redesign its parts and do NOT produce another whole robot or a generic tank-leg robot. Produce a clean two-panel mechanical component study on warm ivory, no text, no logos. LEFT PANEL: RIGHT shoulder assembly ONLY in a true right-side profile, front direction toward image LEFT. Show part of the central chest and the near right upper arm as context. This is the same broad flat bomber wing assembly from the master, viewed edge-on with its lateral wingspan foreshortened, not a thick swept-back bird shoulder pad. The center cockpit/fuselage stays attached to the chest. A separate ivory upper-arm shoulder cap surrounds the core shoulder below the wing. Keep separate a compact orange/black wing-root pivot and the upper-arm shoulder joint: the large wing and its engine are carried by their own bracket, not replacing the core shoulder. The bomber engine is a longitudinal cylinder with its intake pointing FORWARD (image LEFT) just as on the front master. In pure side view we see the SIDE OF THE CYLINDER and a narrow intake lip at its left end, NOT a circular fan facing the viewer, NOT a giant circular pauldron. Keep the graphite upper wing skin, ivory leading edge and orange stripe. The wing is a thin horizontal aircraft surface above the engine; do not turn it into a vertical fin or a thick triangular shoulder shell. No arm-train shell at shoulder. RIGHT PANEL: one RIGHT LEG assembly ONLY from mid-thigh down to foot, in exact matching true right-side profile facing LEFT. Use the actual lower-leg construction visible on the supplied master: a white/ivory core thigh, round dark knee joint, large short steel drill on an orange circular mount projecting FORWARD from the front of the knee, faceted ivory front shin armor, thick orange/black external lower-leg crawler armor, then an articulated ANKLE and a separate heavy armored FOOT with the same white/graphite/orange toe. Preserve a distinct gap/hinge at the ankle: the lower-leg vertical tread armor must end at the calf/ankle module; the foot is a separate module, never one enormous continuous caterpillar belt running from knee around the toe. The foot is a chunky humanoid armored boot with an ivory upper plate, graphite toe block and orange front inset from the master; show a short heel and low outer sole treads, not an elongated triangular tank track. Keep the leg long and the boot modestly longer than the fist, not a boat-shaped slipper. Crawler tread pads and visible round wheel hubs follow the SAME outer-calf placement of the reference, not new thigh treads. Show the side armor profile with only the necessary hidden-depth interpretation, preserve the source's panel/color hierarchy. Drill axis points horizontally forward (LEFT), not sideways at viewer; it is on the KNEE, not hip or ankle. Use the reference's crisp clean KINETIC_CEL animation drawing, confident pressure-varied ink, two-level cel shadow, graphite/ivory/orange blocks, simple material highlights. Orthographic component elevation, camera perfectly at the SIDE, no three-quarter view, no circular front fan visible, no rear view. Both panels share LEFT=FRONT and RIGHT=BACK. Keep all components fully inside frame with margin, evenly spaced panels; no arrows, labels, hands, extra parts or floating duplicates. This is a faithful component interpretation to resolve the master's joints, not a new design.
